The intent below saying how long Alan was away is no reason to expect more or less of him killed the three layoff numbers, taken off the selection policy at 00fe0f1. intentStack.statement: A movement Alan may not perform is gone before any movement is ranked.
Every constraint keeping a movement out names when that constraint is tested again.
The next movement is chosen from what Alan has already done rather than planned as a session.
Whether the next movement is new or familiar is decided by what Alan has already done today.
The most valuable movement available is always the one offered next.
A movement's value is weighed against the goals Alan states rather than training in general.
A movement is dropped when that movement stops progressing rather than after a fixed time.
A dropped movement is offered again once its pattern has progressed elsewhere.
A movement Alan's kit cannot load further is made harder some other way.
A muscle under its weekly set floor is owed work before any muscle above that floor.
A set counts toward the weekly total only where that set was taken near failure.
How Alan is today is read from the sets Alan has just done rather than asked in advance.
The first movement offered is one Alan has done enough to read a drop against.
How long Alan was away is no reason to expect more or less of Alan today.
A movement Alan turns down tells the selector as much as a set Alan finishes.
A movement chosen carries the weight to use and a suggested number of reps.
The goal weights shape how the selector is built rather than scoring each movement.
Every constraint the selector obeys is a predicate over an exercise page.
What Alan owns is read from the kit pages rather than written as a constraint.
